# truenas_directoryservices (Resource)

Manages the TrueNAS directory services configuration (directoryservices.config) — joining the system to an Active Directory domain, an IPA (FreeIPA) domain, or binding to a plain LDAP directory. This is a singleton resource: there is exactly one directory services configuration per TrueNAS system, so it is never created or deleted on TrueNAS; Terraform create/update calls directoryservices.update (a job — joining or leaving a domain can take a while), and after an enabling update this provider additionally polls directoryservices.status until it reports HEALTHY (up to 5 minutes) before considering the apply successful. DELETE NEVER CALLS directoryservices.leave: destroying this resource calls directoryservices.update with enable=false only, which disables directory services locally without leaving the domain or removing the TrueNAS computer account from the domain controller. This is deliberate — leaving a domain requires a domain administrator credential that is not necessarily available (or desirable to hold) at destroy time.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# NOTE: joining Active Directory is disruptive (creates a computer account
# and DNS records on the domain controller). "credential.password" is
# write-only (Terraform >= 1.11 required): it is sent to TrueNAS on
# create/update but never stored in state. Destroying this resource only
# disables directory services locally (enable = false) — it never leaves
# the domain, so the TrueNAS computer account is left in place on the
# domain controller.
resource "truenas_directoryservices" "ad" {
  service_type = "ACTIVEDIRECTORY"
  enable       = true

  credential = {
    credential_type = "KERBEROS_USER"
    username        = "administrator"
    password        = var.ad_join_password
  }

  configuration_activedirectory = {
    hostname = "truenas"
    domain   = "example.internal"

    # Optional: explicit idmap override. Left unset (the default), TrueNAS
    # assigns its own RID-backend ranges on first join and this provider
    # preserves them on every later update.
    idmap = {
      builtin = {
        range_low  = 90000001
        range_high = 100000000
      }
      idmap_domain = {
        idmap_backend = "RID"
        range_low     = 100000001
        range_high    = 200000000
      }
    }
  }
}

variable "ad_join_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# NOTE: LDAP directory services bind to a plain LDAP server rather than
# joining a domain. "credential.bindpw" is write-only (Terraform >= 1.11
# required): sent on create/update but never stored in state. Destroying
# this resource only disables directory services locally (enable = false).
resource "truenas_directoryservices" "ldap" {
  service_type = "LDAP"
  enable       = true

  credential = {
    credential_type = "LDAP_PLAIN"
    binddn          = "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=internal"
    bindpw          = var.ldap_bind_password
  }

  configuration_ldap = {
    server_urls           = ["ldaps://ldap.example.internal"]
    basedn                = "dc=example,dc=internal"
    validate_certificates = true
  }
}

variable "ldap_bind_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# NOTE: joining IPA (FreeIPA) is disruptive in the same way Active
# Directory is (creates a host entry and DNS records on the IPA server).
# "credential.password" is write-only (Terraform >= 1.11 required).
# Destroying this resource only disables directory services locally
# (enable = false) — it never leaves the domain.
resource "truenas_directoryservices" "ipa" {
  service_type = "IPA"
  enable       = true

  credential = {
    credential_type = "KERBEROS_USER"
    username        = "admin"
    password        = var.ipa_join_password
  }

  configuration_ipa = {
    target_server = "ipa.example.internal"
    hostname      = "truenas"
    domain        = "example.internal"
    basedn        = "dc=example,dc=internal"
  }
}

variable "ipa_join_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enable` (Boolean) Enable the directory service. Setting this to true when TrueNAS has never joined the configured domain causes TrueNAS to attempt to join it — creating a computer account and DNS records on the domain controller (ACTIVEDIRECTORY/IPA) or binding to the configured LDAP server (LDAP). Setting this to false disables directory services locally without leaving the domain. Destroying this resource always sends enable=false (see the resource-level description); it never leaves the domain.

### Optional

- `configuration_activedirectory` (Attributes) Active Directory join configuration. REQUIRED whenever "enable" is true and service_type is "ACTIVEDIRECTORY" — see "credential" for why this must be supplied on every apply for as long as enable stays true, not only the first time. "trusted_domains" is not exposed by this provider version — TrueNAS applies its standard default (no trusted domains) on first join, and this provider preserves whatever value TrueNAS has already assigned on every subsequent update. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory))
- `configuration_ipa` (Attributes) IPA (FreeIPA) join configuration. REQUIRED whenever "enable" is true and service_type is "IPA". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ipa))
- `configuration_ldap` (Attributes) Plain LDAP directory configuration. REQUIRED whenever "enable" is true and service_type is "LDAP". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap))
- `credential` (Attributes) Credential used to join the domain or bind to LDAP. REQUIRED the first time "enable" is set to true. For ACTIVEDIRECTORY/IPA it may be omitted from configuration on later applies: once joined, TrueNAS itself swaps the KERBEROS_USER credential used for the join for a keytab-backed KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL machine-account credential internally, and this provider automatically resends THAT (not the original password) on every subsequent update that keeps directory services enabled, including the eventual disable. LDAP credentials (LDAP_PLAIN/LDAP_ANONYMOUS/LDAP_MTLS) have no such swap and must be resupplied (or left in HCL) on every apply. NOTE: credential_type, username, binddn, client_certificate, and principal ARE persisted in Terraform state (none are sensitive on their own); password and bindpw are WriteOnly (Sensitive, requires Terraform >= 1.11) and are NEVER read back from TrueNAS or stored in state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credential))
- `enable_account_cache` (Boolean) Enable backend caching for user and group lists from the directory service. Defaults to true on TrueNAS.
- `enable_dns_updates` (Boolean) Enable automatic DNS updates for the TrueNAS server in the domain via nsupdate and GSSAPI/TSIG. Defaults to true on TrueNAS.
- `kerberos_realm` (String) Name of the Kerberos realm used for authentication to the directory service. When joining Active Directory or IPA for the first time, the realm is normally detected and configured automatically if left unset; not used for LDAP. An empty string clears the assigned realm (null on the wire).
- `service_type` (String) The directory service type to join: "ACTIVEDIRECTORY", "LDAP", or "IPA".
- `timeout` (Number) Timeout (in seconds, 5-60) for DNS queries performed during the join process and for LDAP network requests. Defaults to 10 on TrueNAS.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Fixed identifier for this singleton resource: always "directoryservices".

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_activedirectory`

Required:

- `domain` (String) Full DNS domain name of the Active Directory domain to join (not a domain controller's hostname). Example: "mydomain.internal".
- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the TrueNAS server to register in Active Directory.

Optional:

- `computer_account_ou` (String) Overrides the default organizational unit (OU) in which the TrueNAS computer account is created during the domain join. Example: "TRUENAS_SERVERS/NYC". An empty string clears the override (null on the wire).
- `enable_trusted_domains` (Boolean) Enable support for trusted domains. Defaults to false on TrueNAS. This provider version does not expose per-trusted-domain idmap configuration.
- `idmap` (Attributes) Configuration for mapping Active Directory accounts to accounts on the TrueNAS server. Defaults are suitable for new deployments: when left unset, TrueNAS assigns its own default builtin/idmap_domain ranges (RID backend) on first join, and this provider preserves whatever value TrueNAS has already assigned on every subsequent update. Only the "AD" and "RID" idmap_domain backends are exposed by this provider version — the "LDAP" and "RFC2307" backends (which need a secret LDAP bind password) are deferred. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap))
- `site` (String) The Active Directory site where the TrueNAS server is located. TrueNAS detects this automatically during the join process when left unset. An empty string clears the assigned site (null on the wire).
- `use_default_domain` (Boolean) Controls whether the domain prefix is removed from Active Directory user and group names (e.g. "administrator" instead of "EXAMPLE\administrator"). Defaults to false on TrueNAS.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_activedirectory.idmap`

Optional:

- `builtin` (Attributes) UID and GID range configuration for automatically generated accounts linked to well-known and BUILTIN accounts on Windows servers. Defaults to range 90000001-100000000 on TrueNAS. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap--builtin))
- `idmap_domain` (Attributes) Defines how domain accounts joined to TrueNAS are mapped to Unix UIDs and GIDs. Defaults to the "RID" backend on TrueNAS. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap--idmap_domain))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap--builtin"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_activedirectory.idmap.builtin`

Optional:

- `name` (String) Short name for the domain. Should match the NetBIOS domain name. Null if the domain is configured as the base idmap.
- `range_high` (Number) The highest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.
- `range_low` (Number) The lowest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration_activedirectory--idmap--idmap_domain"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_activedirectory.idmap.idmap_domain`

Required:

- `idmap_backend` (String) Idmap backend type. Only "AD" and "RID" are supported by this provider version ("LDAP" and "RFC2307", which require a secret LDAP bind password, are deferred).

Optional:

- `name` (String) Short name for the domain. Should match the NetBIOS domain name. Null if the domain is configured as the base idmap.
- `range_high` (Number) The highest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.
- `range_low` (Number) The lowest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.
- `schema_mode` (String) Schema mode used to query Active Directory for user/group information. Required when idmap_backend is "AD"; unused otherwise.
- `sssd_compat` (Boolean) RID backend only: generate an idmap low range using the SSSD algorithm. Defaults to false.
- `unix_nss_info` (Boolean) AD backend only: if true, login shell and home directory are retrieved from LDAP SFU attributes. Defaults to false.
- `unix_primary_group` (Boolean) AD backend only: if true, the user's primary group is fetched via the gidNumber LDAP attribute rather than the Active Directory primaryGroupID attribute. Defaults to false.




<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ipa"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ipa`

Required:

- `basedn` (String) The base DN to use when performing LDAP operations. Example: "dc=example,dc=internal".
- `domain` (String) The domain of the IPA server. Example: "ipa.internal".
- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the TrueNAS server to register in IPA during the join process.
- `target_server` (String) The name of the IPA server TrueNAS uses to build URLs when it joins or leaves the IPA domain. Example: "ipa.example.internal".

Optional:

- `smb_domain` (Attributes) Settings for the IPA SMB domain. TrueNAS detects these automatically during the IPA join process; some IPA domains do not include SMB schema configuration, in which case this remains null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ipa--smb_domain))
- `validate_certificates` (Boolean) If false, TrueNAS does not validate certificates from the remote LDAP server. Defaults to true on TrueNAS.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ipa--smb_domain"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ipa.smb_domain`

Optional:

- `domain_name` (String) Name of the SMB domain as defined in the IPA configuration.
- `domain_sid` (String) The domain SID for the IPA domain to which TrueNAS is joined.
- `name` (String) Short name for the SMB domain.
- `range_high` (Number) The highest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.
- `range_low` (Number) The lowest UID or GID that the idmap backend can assign.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap`

Required:

- `basedn` (String) The base DN to use when performing LDAP operations. Example: "dc=domain,dc=internal".
- `server_urls` (List of String) List of LDAP server URIs used for LDAP binds. Each URI must begin with ldap:// or ldaps:// and may use either a DNS name or an IP address. Example: ["ldaps://myldap.domain.internal"].

Optional:

- `attribute_maps` (Attributes) Optional LDAP attribute mapping for LDAP servers that do not follow RFC2307/RFC2307BIS. Use only if the LDAP server is non-standard. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps))
- `auxiliary_parameters` (String) Additional parameters to add to the SSSD configuration. WARNING: TrueNAS does not check the validity of these parameters. An empty string clears the value (null on the wire).
- `schema` (String) The type of LDAP attribute schema the remote LDAP server uses. Defaults to "RFC2307" on TrueNAS.
- `search_bases` (Attributes) Alternative LDAP search base settings, defining where to find user, group, and netgroup entries. If unspecified (the default), TrueNAS uses "basedn" for all three. Use only if the LDAP server uses a non-standard schema. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--search_bases))
- `starttls` (Boolean) Establish TLS by transmitting a StartTLS request to the server. Defaults to false on TrueNAS.
- `validate_certificates` (Boolean) If false, TrueNAS does not validate certificates from the remote LDAP server. Defaults to true on TrueNAS.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.attribute_maps`

Optional:

- `group` (Attributes) LDAP attribute mappings for group entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--group))
- `netgroup` (Attributes) LDAP attribute mappings for netgroup entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--netgroup))
- `passwd` (Attributes) LDAP attribute mappings for user (passwd) entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--passwd))
- `shadow` (Attributes) LDAP attribute mappings for shadow password entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--shadow))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.attribute_maps.group`

Optional:

- `group_gid` (String) The LDAP attribute for the group's id. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `group_member` (String) The LDAP attribute for the names of the group's members. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `group_object_class` (String) The LDAP object class for group entries. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--netgroup"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.attribute_maps.netgroup`

Optional:

- `netgroup_member` (String) The LDAP attribute for the netgroup's members. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `netgroup_object_class` (String) The LDAP object class for netgroup entries. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `netgroup_triple` (String) The LDAP attribute for netgroup triples (host, user, domain). Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--passwd"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.attribute_maps.passwd`

Optional:

- `user_gecos` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's gecos field. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_gid` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's primary group id. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_home_directory` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's home directory. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_name` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's login name. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_object_class` (String) The user entry object class in LDAP. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_shell` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's default shell path. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `user_uid` (String) The LDAP attribute for the user's id. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--attribute_maps--shadow"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.attribute_maps.shadow`

Optional:

- `shadow_expire` (String) shadow(5) account expiration date. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `shadow_inactive` (String) shadow(5) password inactivity period. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `shadow_last_change` (String) shadow(5) date of the last password change. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `shadow_max` (String) shadow(5) maximum password age. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `shadow_min` (String) shadow(5) minimum password age. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.
- `shadow_warning` (String) shadow(5) password warning period. Null (default) uses the RFC2307/RFC2307BIS standard attribute name. An empty string clears an override back to null.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration_ldap--search_bases"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration_ldap.search_bases`

Optional:

- `base_group` (String) Base DN to limit LDAP group searches. Null (default) uses "basedn".
- `base_netgroup` (String) Base DN to limit LDAP netgroup searches. Null (default) uses "basedn".
- `base_user` (String) Base DN to limit LDAP user searches. Null (default) uses "basedn".



<a id="nestedatt--credential"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credential`

Required:

- `credential_type` (String) Credential type. One of "KERBEROS_USER" (username+password — ACTIVEDIRECTORY/IPA join), "KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL" (principal — reuse of an existing machine-account keytab), "LDAP_PLAIN" (binddn+bindpw), "LDAP_ANONYMOUS" (no fields), or "LDAP_MTLS" (client_certificate).

Optional:

- `binddn` (String) Bind DN used to authenticate to the LDAP server. Required when credential_type is "LDAP_PLAIN"; unused otherwise. Example: "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=internal". Not sensitive on its own and persists normally in Terraform state.
- `bindpw` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password for the account named in "binddn". Required when credential_type is "LDAP_PLAIN"; unused otherwise. Write-only: never stored in Terraform state. Requires Terraform >= 1.11.
- `client_certificate` (String) Name of the TrueNAS certificate resource used to authenticate to the LDAP server via mutual TLS. Required when credential_type is "LDAP_MTLS"; unused otherwise.
- `password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password for the account named in "username". Required when credential_type is "KERBEROS_USER"; unused otherwise. Write-only: never stored in Terraform state. Requires Terraform >= 1.11.
- `principal` (String) Kerberos principal for an existing machine-account keytab. Required when credential_type is "KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL"; unused otherwise. This provider sets this automatically on every update after a successful ACTIVEDIRECTORY/IPA join — supplying it directly is normally only needed when re-adopting a join TrueNAS already performed outside Terraform.
- `username` (String) Username of the domain account used to obtain a Kerberos ticket for joining/authenticating to the directory service. Required when credential_type is "KERBEROS_USER"; unused otherwise. This account must exist on the domain controller and (for the initial join) typically needs domain administrator privileges.
